items.title: Labarbera interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2021
items.q: Toots Mondello books you know, so we had all of these transcribed solos that he would give us to read.

ctx.x: What was the set list like at that time? You probably were playing Swing Era tunes but also maybe whatever was on the radio?

Swing and pop music of the day, Glenn Miller stocks, a lot of them were stock arrangements, a lot of Italian tunes. If it was Italian weddings we had to play all of the traditional Italian mazurkas and polkas. And so he had a whole library of that Italian music. And then the pop music of the day you know, which was in the 50s, and a lot of the stuff was — you had some funny stuff — but a lot of it was swing. He had quite a few stocks from the 30s and 40s basically, because he had his own dance band at one time so…
At some point did your father say, especially to you and John on trumpet, that, okay now it’s time to play music that’s not on the page, and how did he describe that?
